description: Our team is tackling the 'Lunar Landing Site Navigator' challenge by building a low-code interactive platform. Our mission is to simplify complex NASA geographic and environmental lunar datasets into a highly intuitive, visual dashboard. Designed with accessible UI/UX, our tool empowers future astronauts, scientists, and space enthusiasts to easily filter, compare, and navigate optimal landing zones on the Moon based on terrain safety, lighting, and resource availability.
summary:
LUNA NAV is an interactive lunar exploration and mission-planning platform developed to support the exploration of potential landing regions near the Moon’s south pole. It brings NASA lunar imagery, topographic data and preliminary mission-planning tools together in one accessible workspace.
Using imagery from NASA Moon Trek and elevation and slope datasets from the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA), users can explore the lunar surface, select candidate locations, examine available terrain information and compare potential landing sites. The platform also includes distance and traverse calculations, preliminary solar and Earth visibility estimates, an interactive candidate comparison system, a research assistant and downloadable reports.
LUNA NAV addresses the challenge of making complex lunar data easier to explore and interpret by connecting scientific information with practical mission-planning tools. Its evidence-based approach distinguishes retrieved measurements from calculated estimates and unavailable data, helping users understand both the possibilities and limitations of their analysis.
The project aims to make lunar exploration more accessible and support informed, transparent planning for future lunar missions.
details:
LUNA NAV is an interactive lunar exploration and preliminary mission-planning platform focused on potential landing regions near the Moon’s south pole. It brings lunar imagery, topographic information, and mission-planning tools together in one workspace.

Users can explore the lunar surface through an interactive map, select candidate landing coordinates, examine available elevation and slope information, and compare potential sites. The platform also includes traverse-distance calculations, preliminary solar and Earth visibility estimates, candidate comparison tools, a research assistant, and downloadable reports and datasets. It uses NASA lunar imagery and data sources, including NASA Moon Trek and the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA).

The project aims to make complex lunar data easier to access, understand, and compare. It can help students, researchers, and space enthusiasts explore the challenges of lunar south-pole missions and investigate potential landing regions. Its intended impact is to encourage accessible, transparent, and data-informed lunar exploration.

LUNA NAV was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with web-mapping tools and NASA data services. The application is designed to run in a web browser without specialised hardware. Its local data storage and export features support convenient exploration and comparison.

The creative aspect of LUNA NAV is the integration of scientific lunar information with practical mission-planning features in a single interactive platform. During development, we considered usability, mobile accessibility, data availability, coordinate accuracy, terrain safety factors, transparency, and the limitations of remote scientific datasets. We distinguish retrieved measurements from calculated estimates and unavailable information so users can understand the reliability of the results.

LUNA NAV is a preliminary exploration and planning tool, not a certified lunar landing safety system.
